headline_marked: [[Bangladesh bows out of Women's Asia Cup T20]] after 40-run semi-final defeat to India
headline: Bangladesh bows out of Women's Asia Cup T20 after 40-run semi-final defeat to India
summary: Bangladesh's campaign in the Women's Asia Cup T20 ended in Dubai after a disappointing performance led to a 40-run loss against India in the first semi-final.
details: Bangladesh's journey in the Women's Asia Cup T20 concluded with a 40-run defeat to India in the first semi-final held in Dubai on Thursday. A disappointing effort across all three departments saw them exit the regional competition.

India, after being asked to bat first, posted a competitive total of 149 for six. They added 53 runs in the final five overs, finishing strongly despite Bangladesh keeping their batters in check until the 15th over.

Shafali Verma was the top-scorer for India with 64 off 40 balls, capitalizing on several reprieves. Harmanpreet Kaur (24 not out), Richa Ghosh (21), and Deepti Sharma (13 not out off six) provided crucial late impetus.
For Bangladesh, Sultana Khatun claimed two wickets for 30 runs. Marufa Akter, Nahida Akter, and Rabeya Khan each secured one wicket.

Bangladesh's chase of 150 runs never gained momentum, with batters seemingly more focused on avoiding a heavy defeat than seriously pursuing the target. They eventually finished on 109 for seven in their 20 overs.

Shorna Akter remained unbeaten on 22 off 18 balls, but by then the match was already out of reach. Top-order batters like Dilara Akter (21), Juaraiya Ferdous (14), and Sobhana Mostary (18) failed to convert their starts.

Captain Nigar Sultana Joty also struggled, scoring 19 off 17 balls, and ended a disappointing tournament with just 56 runs from four matches. Deepti Sharma was the pick of the Indian bowlers, taking 3-26, while Nandani Sharma claimed two wickets.

This defeat marks Bangladesh's ninth consecutive loss to India in T20Is, a streak dating back to September 2023. Bangladesh also lost to India in the semi-final of the previous edition of the Asia Cup.
Seven-time champions India will now advance to Sunday's final at the same venue. They will face either Sri Lanka or Pakistan as they aim to reclaim the title they lost to Sri Lanka in 2024.

headline_marked: [[Dengue claims six lives]] in 24 hours, 1,492 new hospitalizations reported
headline: Dengue claims six lives in 24 hours, 1,492 new hospitalizations reported
summary: Bangladesh has recorded six new Dengue deaths and 1,492 hospitalizations in the last 24 hours, bringing the total death toll this year to 139 and total cases to 48,430.
details: Bangladesh reported six new Dengue deaths and 1,492 hospitalizations in the 24 hours between Wednesday 8 AM and Thursday 8 AM.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) released this information in a report on Thursday, September 10.

According to the DGHS, the total number of Dengue-related deaths in the country this year has now reached 139. The cumulative number of patients admitted to hospitals due to Dengue has risen to 48,430.
